pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Delaware Journeyperson Electrician exam is administered by Prov, Inc. for licensing through the Delaware Division of Professional Regulation. The exam is computer-based, open book, and timed. The Delaware journeyperson electrician examination includes 70 questions and allows 3 hours of testing time. The passing score for Delaware electrician examinations is 75%. Exam results are provided after completion, and results are also reported to the Delaware Division of Professional Regulation. Candidates who need to retake the exam may do so after waiting at least seven days from the previous test attempt. The Delaware Journeyperson Electrician exam content outline includes general electrical theory and principles, plan reading, equipment for general use, motors and controls, wiring and protection, wiring methods and materials, communication systems, special conditions, special equipment, and special occupancies.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Delaware Journeyperson Electrician exam is an open book test. Candidates may use approved reference books during testing, but all reference materials must follow the exam provider’s rules. The candidate information bulletin states that exams are open book and timed, and it also lists reference materials that may be used during testing. Reference-book preparation is important because open book does not mean the answers will be easy to find. Candidates need to know where common topics are located, how code articles are organized, how tables are used, and how to move through the NEC efficiently under timed conditions. The included National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs is intended to help candidates build that navigation skill during study. Prov’s reference material rules prohibit handwritten notes in reference books. Moveable tabs and Post-it notes are not permitted, photocopied reference books are not permitted, and test preparation study guides are not approved references in the testing center.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Delaware journeyperson electrician licensing is handled through the Delaware Division of Professional Regulation’s DELPROS online system. Candidates may apply through different pathways, including examination, reciprocity, or certification, depending on their background and documentation. A candidate applying by examination must submit the required application materials through DELPROS and pass the journeyperson examination. Delaware also provides a certificate pathway for applicants who hold a certificate of completion issued by the Department of Labor or an approved apprenticeship program in Delaware, another state, a U.S. territory, or the District of Columbia. Reciprocity may be available for applicants who hold a current journeyperson license from another state, U.S. territory, or the District of Columbia, depending on the Board’s review of substantially similar licensing requirements and experience.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Delaware requires individuals who perform electrical services in the state to hold the proper Delaware professional electrician license. The Board defines electrical services or electrical work as activity covered by the National Electrical Code as adopted by the Delaware State Fire Commission. A Delaware Journeyperson Electrician license allows the holder to perform electrical services under supervision while gaining additional experience and developing the skills needed for higher-level electrician license classifications. Delaware’s electrician license types include apprentice, residential, journeyperson, master, master special, limited, and limited special classifications. For examination applicants, Delaware requires Verification of Employment forms showing at least 8,000 hours of full-time experience performing electrical work under the supervision of a licensed master electrician, master electrician special, limited electrician, or limited electrician special.

pieces.t: Delaware Master Electrician candidates begin by applying through DELPROS, the Delaware Professional Regulation Online Services portal. A candidate must create a DELPROS user account, begin the correct license application, submit the required application materials, and receive approval from the Board of Electrical Examiners before sitting for the examination. pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: For Delaware experience obtained after June 30, 2012, the candidate must have been licensed as an Apprentice Electrician or Journeyperson Electrician at the time for that experience to be credited. After the Board reviews and approves the application, the candidate receives notice of approval to sit for the exam. ProV then provides the examination registration information. Candidates schedule their exam through ProV and may test in person at available testing locations or through approved online testing when eligible. Candidates should follow all scheduling, identification, reference-material, and test-day rules listed by ProV. After passing the examination, Master Electrician applicants must submit proof of general liability insurance of at least $300,000. The applicant’s name must appear on the insurance document, even when coverage is provided through an employer’s policy. Once the Board office receives the passing score and confirms that the applicant has met all licensing requirements, the license may be issued.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Delaware requires a professional electrician license to perform electrical services in the state. Delaware defines electrical services or electrical work as activity covered by the National Electrical Code as adopted by the Delaware State Fire Commission. The Delaware Board of Electrical Examiners recognizes several license categories, including Master Electrician, Limited Electrician, Master Electrician Special, Limited Electrician Special, Journeyperson Electrician, Residential Electrician, and Apprentice Electrician. The Master Electrician license is the broad statewide license associated with planning, estimating, laying out, performing, or supervising electrical installation and repair work for lighting, heating, or power in structures. Candidates who do not qualify for the full Master Electrician license but have knowledge in a specialty area may apply for a Master Electrician Special license in approved specialty areas such as electric signs, elevators, HVAC, primary distribution systems, pools, or refrigeration.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Delaware also allows application by reciprocity for applicants who hold a current license of the same type from another state, United States territory, or the District of Columbia. Reciprocity requirements depend on whether the Board has determined that the other jurisdiction’s licensing standards are substantially similar to Delaware’s standards. Applicants applying by reciprocity may need to submit license verifications and, in some cases, proof of experience. Master and Limited Electrician applicants must provide proof of general liability insurance of at least $300,000 before the license can be issued. Applicants may take the exam before submitting proof of insurance, but the license cannot be issued until the Board receives acceptable proof. Electricians should also monitor renewal and continuing education requirements after licensure.

pieces.t: This Ultimate Combo gives Delaware candidates multiple ways to prepare. The Delaware Master Electrician Study Guide supports broad review of state exam content areas. pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials
pieces.t: Calculations should be practiced throughout the study process. Electrical calculation questions often require candidates to identify the correct formula, use the proper NEC table, convert units accurately, and check the answer for reasonableness. Working calculations repeatedly helps candidates improve both speed and accuracy. Code navigation should also be part of every study session. Candidates should practice using the table of contents, index, definitions, article structure, tables, notes, exceptions, and cross-references. During an open-book exam, the strongest candidates are not simply searching from scratch. They understand how the code book is organized and can move through it with purpose. Flash cards are useful for shorter study sessions and repeated review. They help candidates reinforce terminology, formulas, code concepts, and trade knowledge when they do not have time for a full practice exam. The Online Test Success Kit adds another layer of preparation by helping candidates apply what they have studied through exam-style questions and review.
